Chapter 0390 BPMOUTPUT

The Wire Choir

The right song, at the right moment, out of somebody else's window.

Look up in an East Van lane: poles, layers of wires, trolley lines, transformers. Add every radio, every car stereo, every pair of headphones and the bass leaking under a warehouse door, and you have the Wire Choir. It is how Terminal City sings to itself. When a neighbourhood goes quiet the Choir leans on coincidence: somebody's car at a red light playing the exact song, a band rehearsing through a wall you happen to be leaning on, a window left open. You still choose what you listen to. You really did. The timing was just a little too good. No one hears the broadcast as an announcement.

At a laundromat, the Cyclist notices three listeners giving up on the same unfinished musical phrase. A radio on the counter dissolves into hiss just before its last few notes. Outside, a wire shadow stops short of an old ink mark beside the window. The Cyclist tries to join the two with a small adhesive print, but a passing bus fills the glass with reflections and the alignment disappears. She waits, shifts her position and places the print where the shadow actually falls. Inside, the phrase makes it to the end. A person folding a sheet begins humming a different ending of their own. The Cyclist pockets the backing paper and walks her bicycle away; nobody has received instructions about what to like.

The ruleNo one hears the broadcast as an announcement.

Terminal City · Storybook v0.10.0 · built 2026-09-13
Terminal City is an original fictional mythology inspired by Vancouver’s geography, weather, wildlife, infrastructure, art, and electronic music. It makes no claim to historical, Indigenous, or religious tradition. Real places are used as settings; the operating system layered on them is invented.
Made by Steve Hiehn, a software developer and electronic musician based in Vancouver, Canada. All music was created using a custom DAW, Signals & Sorcery.
